An app for the Ableton Move

CONSOLE.

An 8-track tape recorder and groovebox for the Ableton Move.

  • Sequence eight drum and synth tracks.
  • Dozens of synths, drums, and inserts.
  • Parameter locks and step components.
  • Layout patterns in Song mode.
  • Record, splice, cut, and drop to eight tape tracks.
  • Export final bounces and grab via browser.
  • Mirror the screen to any web browser.
Get started See how it works Move firmware 2.1.1 · November 2026

Mirror the screen to your phone or computer for more detailed visualizations.

The tape

Eight tracks. Real splices.

Record on a track, then edit it the way you would on a tape machine.

Arm and record

Tracks can be mono or stereo. Inputs can be individual drums or whole kits. 

Splice, copy, cut

Splice, lift, and drop where you want.
Multiple splices can be lifted and merged before being dropped to one track.

Loop and overdub

Set in and out points with the arrow keys, loop between them, and switch between replacing the tape and adding to it.

Bounce

Tracks can be exported as wav, aiff, flac, m4a and collected via a local webpage. Stems and final mix are automatically exported.

Drum machines

The left 4 × 4 pads are the drums. The right 4 × 4 pads play the drum chromatically.

Synths

Scroll through pages of parameters, lfos, inserts, and arp

sampler

The sampler can load up to 5 samples per drum. Load two samples and use the blend parameter to fade between. Set to random and load up to 5 samples that play back randomly.

Sequencer

Sixteen steps, no limits on feel

Every instrument has its own sequencer. Every drum has its own sequencer. Every note can have its own sequencer.

Per-lane rate

Each drum runs at its own rate, length, and Euclidean fills.

Step COMPONENTS

Hold a step to lock velocity, chance, hold, pulse or length on just that hit.

Triplets

One menu setting turns the grid into triplets. LFOs and the arp have triplet rates too.

LFOs and arp

Two LFOs per pattern and an arpeggiator.

Effects

What you hear is what you record

Each instrument has a reverb and delay send, as well as two insert effects.
Two more global inserts can be added, and everything gets recorded onto tape. Tape tracks can be mono or stereo, inputs can be individual drums or the whole kit or synth.

  • Reverb
  • Delay
  • Insert 1
  • Insert 2
  • Song insert 1
  • Song insert 2
External screen

Your phone is the big screen

Connect to a locally-hosted webpage to see a much bigger and higher-res UI environment. No apps to download, you can use your phone, laptop, tablet, any device that has a web browser.

Getting started

Five steps to Console

Installing Console onto the Move is easy.

  1. Allow your computer to connect

    On your computer, open Terminal (Mac) or PowerShell (Windows). Make a key by running this. Skip it if you already have a key.

    ssh-keygen -t ed25519

    Now enter this-

    Maccat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
    Windowstype $env:USERPROFILE\.ssh\id_ed25519.pub

    Terminal will print out the key, copy it. Head over to move.local/development/ssh and paste the key.

  2. Install

    You need RNBO Move Takeover on your Move first.
    https://cycling74.com/releases/rnbo-move/1.4.5-alpha.0

    Then paste this into Terminal on your computer and wait a few minutes.

    ssh ableton@move.local "python3 -c 'import sys,urllib.request as u;exec(u.urlopen(sys.argv[1]).read())' https://raw.githubusercontent.com/briwil/console-move/main/move/install.py"


  3. Start Console

    Hold Shift and press Step 2 to open the Move's settings, then choose RNBO at the bottom of the list. Takes a few seconds, be patient.

  4. Press Record

    Pick your instruments. Play, live record, or sequence.
    Switch to tape mode, arm your tracks and record your tracks.
    Splice, lift, drop. A final wav file is written after every edit.

  5. Bounce and quit

    Bounce your tracks, grab them at http://move.local:8080/files and quit back to the original Move OS when you're done.
    No harm, no foul.
